mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional triggers.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2% (12-month rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.2% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.2%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances (3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (12-month rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 105.0), supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits face headwinds.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 105.0, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods (3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 240 signals accelerating inflation, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 240, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) relative to the previous year correlates with rising corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional triggers.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth fails to predict positive SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods (12-month rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative SPX 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases (12-month rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong housing starts (HOUST above 1200.0), the housing sector's contribution to GDP growth drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as construction activity boosts related industries.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1200.0, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods (3-year rolling window).
